newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GIANTS ACQUIRE ALVAREZ, HERNANDEZ FROM DIVESTING CHISOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GIANTS ACQUIRE ALVAREZ, HERNANDEZ FROM DIVESTING CHISOX.

text.p: The Chicago White Sox -- just 3 1/2 games off the lead in the American League Central -- continued their shocking housecleaning Thursday by sending starters Wilson Alvarez and Danny Darwin plus closer Roberto Hernandez to the San Francisco Giants for six minor-leaguers.

In return for the high-profile trio, the White Sox received shortstop Mike Caruso, outfielder Brian Manning and pitchers Lorenzo Barcelo, Keith Foulke, Bob Howry and Ken Vining from the National League West-leading Giants.

Earlier this week, Chicago dealt designated hitter Harold Baines to the Baltimore Orioles for a player to be named later, making White Sox veteran shortstop Ozzie Guillen so angry that he smashed a TV set in the clubhouse.

Chicago's dramatic downsizing comes on the heels of an off-season of vigorous spending by the White Sox, who landed superstar outfielder Albert Belle, who is making $10 million this season, as well as pitchers Doug Drabek, Jaime Navarro, Roger McDowell and Darwin.
Alvarez and Hernandez are both in the final year of their contracts and will command big money on the free-agent market.

Alvarez (9-8) was the ace of the White Sox staff, leading the club in wins and strikeouts (110). He had a 3.03 ERA in 22 starts. The 27-year-old left-hander was in his seventh year with Chicago after beginning his career in Texas.
Hernandez was also in his seventh year with the White Sox and fifth as their closer. He is 5-1 with 27 saves and a 2.44 ERA in 46 appearances, spanning 48 innings.

The 41-year-old Darwin (4-8) started 17 games for Chicago, recording 62 strikeouts and 31 walks with a 4.13 ERA over 113 1/3 innings. He is in his 20th major-league season, having played previously with Texas, Milwaukee, Houston, Boston, Toronto and Pittsburgh.

The Giants are in first place in the National League West, but were desperately searching for pitching help. They have lost 13 of their last 21 games and seen their lead over the second-place Los Angeles Dodgers shrink to just one-half game.
The Giants have lost 5 1/2 games off their lead since the All-Star break.
Hernandez likely will move into a set-up role with San Francisco, as Rod Beck leads the majors with 32 saves.
Alvarez and Darwin will join Shawn Estes, Mark Gardner and Kirk Rueter in the Giants rotation.
